response.sql:
WITH invoice_orders_by_gender AS (
  SELECT 
    c.gender,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) as invoiced_order_count
  FROM Invoices i
  JOIN Orders o ON i.order_id = o.order_id
  JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  GROUP BY c.gender
),
gender_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    gender,
    invoiced_order_count,
    AVG(invoiced_order_count) OVER () as overall_avg
  FROM invoice_orders_by_gender
)
SELECT 
  AVG(invoiced_order_count) as avg_invoiced_order_count,
  AVG(invoiced_order_count - overall_avg) as avg_excess_over_overall_avg
FROM gender_stats
WHERE invoiced_order_count > overall_avg;

assumptions.assumption: An order may have multiple invoices; distinct orders per gender is used to avoid double-counting. If an order has 2 invoices, it counts as 1 invoiced order for that gender, not 2.
The 'overall per-gender average' is computed from all genders before filtering, not recalculated from only the above-average genders.
